children.text: If you're a property owner or manager, you know how important it is to keep your utility costs under control. One of the most effective ways to do this is by installing water sub meters. By measuring the water usage of individual units within a building, you can accurately bill tenants for their usage, promote water conservation, and increase efficiency.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we specialize in sub-metering for a diverse range of real estate investments. Our water sub meters are designed to help you save money and reduce waste. With our state-of-the-art meters, you'll be able to accurately measure water usage and bill tenants accordingly. This promotes fairness and transparency and encourages tenants to conserve water.

Our water sub meters have proven to be highly effective in helping property owners and managers reduce costs and increase efficiency. In fact, our metrics show that on average, our clients see a 32% increase in property value and an 18% reduction in operating costs. Plus, we're 100% regulatory compliant, so you can rest assured that you're getting the best possible service.
Understanding Water Sub Meters
If you own a multi-tenant property or manage a commercial building, understanding water submeters is critical to managing utility costs and ensuring fair billing practices. Learn more about
water submetering solutions

. Water submeters are additional meters installed on individual water lines within a property or premises, allowing for the measurement and tracking of water usage for specific units, tenants, or areas within a larger property.
Types of Water Sub Meters

There are two main types of water sub meters: digital display and pulse output meters. Digital display meters provide a clear readout of water usage and are ideal for properties that require accurate, real-time data. Pulse output meters, on the other hand, send a signal to a remote device that records water usage data. These meters are typically less expensive than digital display meters and are ideal for properties that require basic water usage data.
Benefits of Submetering

Water submetering has many benefits for property owners and managers. By installing submeters, you can accurately track water usage and allocate costs to tenants based on actual consumption. This promotes fairness and transparency in billing practices and can help reduce disputes between tenants and property owners. Additionally, submetering can help identify leaks or other water usage issues, allowing for prompt repairs and cost savings.

As a leading provider of water submeters, Axis Meter Solutions is the best option for utility management. Our team of specialists has experience in sub-metering for a diverse range of real estate investments and can help you implement a submetering system that meets your specific needs. Our metrics include a 32% average property value increase, 18% lower operating costs, and we're 100% regulatory compliant. Contact us today to learn more about how we can help you save money and streamline your utility management processes.
The Installation Process

Installing water sub meters is an essential step towards managing utility costs and improving the efficiency of your property. The installation process involves two main stages: planning and preparation, and step-by-step installation. In this section, we will guide you through the process of installing water sub meters, and explain why Axis Meter Solutions is the best option for utility management.
Planning and Preparation

Before installing water sub meters, it is crucial to plan and prepare for the installation process. This involves assessing the compatibility of your property's plumbing system with the sub meters. At Axis Meter Solutions, we offer a comprehensive plumbing assessment to ensure that your property is compatible with our sub meters.

The next step is to determine the number of sub meters required for your property. This is based on the number of units and the layout of your property. Our team of specialists will work with you to determine the appropriate number of sub meters required for your property.
Step-by-Step Installation Guide

Once the planning and preparation stage is complete, the next step is to install the water sub meters. At Axis Meter Solutions, we follow a step-by-step installation guide to ensure that the installation process is seamless and efficient.

The first step is to install the couplings and flow tubes during the rough-in plumbing stage. Spacer tubes are installed in place of the meters during the flushing and pressure-testing process. This is to prevent damage to the meters during pressure testing.
Once the plumbing system has been flushed and pressure-tested, the sub meters are installed. Our team of specialists will ensure that the sub meters are installed correctly and are fully functional.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we are specialists in sub-metering for a diverse range of real estate investments. Our metrics include a 32% average property value increase, 18% lower operating costs, and we are 100% regulatory compliant. Trust us to provide you with the best utility management solution for your property.
Billing and Cost Management
Accurate Billing and Fairness

Billing for water consumption can be a challenging process for landlords and tenants alike. Without sub-meters, tenants may be charged a flat rate or an estimate of their water usage, which can lead to disputes over fairness and accuracy. However, with sub-meters, each tenant is responsible for their individual usage, and billing is based on actual consumption, promoting fairness and transparency. This ensures that tenants only pay for the water they use, which can result in lower bills and a more equitable distribution of costs.

Our sub-metering solutions ensure accurate billing and promote fairness between landlords and tenants. Our team of experts will work with you to design a customized sub-metering system that meets your specific needs and requirements. We will also handle the installation and maintenance of the system, ensuring that it is always functioning properly.

Regulatory Compliance and Legal Considerations

When it comes to sub-metering water usage, regulatory compliance and legal considerations are essential. As a property owner, it is your responsibility to ensure that you comply with state regulations and requirements. Failure to do so can result in hefty fines and legal action.
State Regulations and Requirements

Each state has its own regulations and requirements for water sub-metering, so it's important to familiarize yourself with the laws in your state. For example, in Washington state, property owners are required to provide tenants with a sub-metering system that accurately measures water usage. In Illinois, sub-metering is allowed but must comply with specific requirements. In Wisconsin, sub-metering is allowed but only for multifamily buildings with four or more units.

Other states, such as Pennsylvania, Nevada, Georgia, Oklahoma, and New Hampshire, have varying regulations and requirements for water sub-metering. It's important to research and understand the laws in your state to ensure compliance.
Ensuring Compliance for Property Owners
As a property owner, it's important to ensure compliance with state regulations and requirements. One way to do this is by working with a reputable sub-metering company like Axis Meter Solutions.

Axis Meter Solutions is a specialist in sub-metering for a diverse range of real estate investments. Our metrics include a 32% average property value increase, 18% lower operating costs, and we're 100% regulatory compliant. By working with us, you can ensure that your property is in compliance with state regulations and requirements.

In addition to working with a reputable sub-metering company, property owners should also keep accurate records of water usage, ensure that sub-meters are installed and maintained correctly, and provide tenants with clear and accurate billing statements. By following these guidelines, property owners can ensure compliance with state regulations and requirements while also providing tenants with a fair and accurate billing system.

These solutions typically include a range of features, such as wifi or ethernet connectivity, transceivers, and mobile apps, which allow users to track and monitor their water usage in real-time.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we offer a range of smart metering solutions that are designed to meet the needs of a diverse range of real estate investments. Our smart meters are highly accurate, easy to install, and can be integrated with a range of other systems, such as building automation systems and energy management systems.
Leveraging Technology for Leak Detection

One of the key benefits of smart metering solutions is their ability to help property owners and managers detect leaks in their water systems. By monitoring water usage in real-time, smart metering solutions can quickly identify unusual patterns in water usage that may be indicative of a leak.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we offer a range of leak detection tools that are designed to work seamlessly with our smart metering solutions. These tools use advanced algorithms to analyze water usage data and identify potential leaks, allowing property owners and managers to take action before the problem becomes more serious.

Overall, if you're looking for the best option for Utility Management, Axis Meter Solutions is the clear choice. Our smart metering solutions are designed to help you reduce your water usage, lower your operating costs, and ensure that you remain 100% regulatory compliant. With a 32% average property value increase and 18% lower operating costs, our solutions are the perfect choice for property owners and managers who want to take their water management to the next level.

Sub-metering has been proven to be a successful strategy for reducing utility costs and increasing property value in multi-unit properties and apartment complexes. By installing sub-meters in residential units, tenants are held responsible for their individual water consumption, which promotes water conservation and reduces overall water usage. This leads to lower utility bills for both the property owner and the tenants.
